title: Any recommendations for an AI-powered Unity development workflow?
author: RealMiniBU
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been working on my game project for about six months now, and I'm still struggling to establish an efficient AI-assisted development workflow.

Do you guys have any recommendations for multi-agent workflows or unified development environments that could help streamline the process?

I'm developing my game in Unity and currently using Codex for coding and Meshy AI for 3D asset generation.

I'd love to hear about your setups, tools, and experiences. What actually works for you?

replies.author: RealMiniBU
replies.body: Do you use some kind of unified interface to manage all of this, or do you just work with separate desktop apps and the terminal?

replies.author: oSi7ENT
replies.body: It depends, I use antigravity for cli workflow through unity, but a lot of my tools are custom made to interface with one another

replies.author: RealMiniBU
replies.body:
I'm currently trying to build a more unified workflow using Traycer.

I keep looking at the quality of games other indie devs are making, and honestly, it gets pretty discouraging when I compare them to my own project.

That's why I've started looking into integrating the best AI tools available and building a proper, unified development stack, rather than just relying on Codex with a few MCP servers connected to it.

I'm trying to figure out how to bring everything together into one efficient workflow, especially when it comes to improving the visual quality of my game.

replies.author: oSi7ENT
replies.body: Here’s the secret. It’s a slow process at first. Over 3 weeks of under the hood actions. Took over 4 hours last night on one guard tower alone, with extreme attention to detail…. But once you get those going, the process goes faster and faster

comments.author: RealMiniBU
comments.body:
I already have a working prototype with a playable build. It even has visuals in place, and most of the core mechanics are already implemented.

My biggest challenges right now are the UI and the overall visual quality of the game, including 3D assets, animations, VFX, polish, and all that stuff.

I'm pretty optimistic, though! I think we'll figure it all out, get everything looking great, and eventually ship the game!
